pr.title: Allow GVN to produce places and not just locals.
pr.description:
That may be too big of a hammer, as we may introduce new deref projections (possible UB footgun + probably not good for perf).

The second commit opts out of introducing projections that don't have a stable offset, which is probably what we want. Hence no new Deref and no new Index projections.

Fixes https://github.com/rust-lang/rust/issues/138936

pr.author: cjgillot

processing.reason: The merged historical change is semantically value-preserving on the regression case. Before GVN, the MIR computes `_3 = &_1[_4]`, then `_9 = copy (*_3)`; after GVN it computes `_9 = copy _1[0 of 1]` only because `_4` is the constant `0` and the projection is a stable array offset. Both read the same element of `_1`, so no defined-execution value difference can exist. The patch also explicitly passes `allow_complex_projection = false` for `try_as_operand` and `visit_rvalue`, rejecting the only kind of place replacement (new `Deref` or dynamic `Index` projections) that could observe a changed index/pointer value. That unguarded variant was the PR's first commit, not the merged historical transformation; encoding it would require modeling an intermediate implementation that the final patch specifically removes. `simplify_aggregate` retains the old complex-projection behavior rather than introducing a new one. Therefore no source-grounded original-vs-incorrect pair can be validated without manufacturing the rejected intermediate rewrite.

analysis.originalLogic: Before this PR, GVN's operand and rvalue substitution only asked for a whole local: `try_as_operand` used `else if let Some(local) = self.try_as_local(index, location) { ... Some(Operand::Copy(local.into())) }`, and `VnState::visit_rvalue` used `else if let Some(local) = self.try_as_local(value, location) && *rvalue != Rvalue::Use(Operand::Move(local.into())) { *rvalue = Rvalue::Use(Operand::Copy(local.into())); ... }`. `simplify_aggregate` had a separate loop that could walk `Value::Projection` and construct a projected place for aggregate reconstruction, but general operand/rvalue replacement could not use such a place.
analysis.incorrectTransformation: The historically limited transformation replaced a value only with `Copy(local.into())`, so an equivalent stable-offset projection such as `_1[0 of 1]` was not used and the deref form `_9 = copy (*_3)` remained. The PR also guards against the opposite mistake: when materializing a place for general operand/rvalue replacement, it must not introduce arbitrary projections, because walking projection values without checking offset stability can create new `Deref`/non-stable `Index` projections, described as a "possible UB footgun + probably not good for perf." The corrected rewrite calls `try_as_place(index, location, false)` and requires `(allow_complex_projection || proj.is_stable_offset())`; only aggregate reconstruction passes `true`.
analysis.inputDomain: MIR where GVN has a value index equal to a projection chain rooted at a local that strictly dominates the use location, and the projected place has the same type as the value being replaced. The regression test uses inlined `Ord::cmp(&x[0], &y[0])` on `[i32; 1]` arguments, where the input MIR contains `_9 = copy (*_3)` and `_10 = copy (*_6)` and GVN can instead use `copy _1[0 of 1]` and `copy _2[0 of 1]`. The same logic applies to `simplify_aggregate`, which allows non-constant offsets because that is still better than reconstructing an aggregate.
analysis.summary: GVN was generalized from replacing operands/rvalues only with dominant locals to replacing them with places built from projection chains, while explicitly refusing to introduce projections without stable offsets in general operand/rvalue contexts. Stable projections such as constant array indexes are allowed and produce `copy _1[0 of 1]`; complex projections such as `Deref` or dynamic `Index` are not newly introduced there. This PR says it fixes rust-lang/rust#138936 and adds a MIR regression test.
analysis.trigger: GVN simplifies an operand or rvalue and the value index can be traced through `Value::Projection` nodes to a dominating local. If every projection is stable (for example a constant array index or field projection), `try_as_place(..., false)` may construct the projected place and replace the operand/rvalue with `Operand::Copy(place)`. If a projection is not a stable offset, the general operand/rvalue path must return `None` rather than introduce a new `Deref`/non-stable `Index` projection.
preconditions: GVN has a `VnIndex` whose value is a projection chain rooted at a local.
The base local strictly dominates the use location; `try_as_place` documents that all locals in the place strictly dominate `loc`.
The type of the constructed place matches the type of the original rvalue/value (`rvalue.ty(...) == place.ty(...).ty` in `simplify_aggregate`).
For `try_as_operand` and `visit_rvalue`, every projection must satisfy `proj.is_stable_offset()`; `allow_complex_projection` is `false`.
For `simplify_aggregate`, `allow_complex_projection` is `true` because a projected place with non-constant offsets is still considered better than reconstructing an aggregate.
Any reused place's base local must be inserted into `reused_locals` so storage statements can be removed.
`visit_rvalue` avoids rewriting when the rvalue is already `Use(Operand::Move(place))` or `Use(Operand::Copy(place))`.
pitfalls: Do not treat all place-producing paths the same: `simplify_aggregate` passes `allow_complex_projection=true`, while `try_as_operand` and `visit_rvalue` pass `false`.

A constant array index such as `_1[0 of 1]` is a stable offset and is intentionally allowed; the PR's warning is about projections without a stable offset, such as new `Deref` or dynamic `Index` projections.
Do not conflate this choice with borrowing rules: the patch checks type equality, dominance, and offset stability; it does not add a general borrow-checker condition.
The MIR test diff's `-` lines are the input before GVN and the `+` lines are the output after GVN; the new test explicitly forbids deref projections with `CHECK-NOT: (*{{_.*}});`.
Replacing a value with a projected place requires marking the base local reused; otherwise storage statements remain in the MIR.
No compiler was built or executed for this analysis; do not claim reproduction or runtime behavior.
analysis.testStrategy: Add a `tests/mir-opt` test with `EMIT_MIR_FOR_EACH_PANIC_STRATEGY` and an `EMIT_MIR ...GVN.diff` directive. Use a function such as `compare_constant_index(x: [i32; 1], y: [i32; 1]) -> Ordering` returning `Ord::cmp(&x[0], &y[0])`. In the CHECK lines, assert no deref projections with `CHECK-NOT: (*{{_.*}});`, then assert the stable projected copies: `[[lhs:_.*]] = copy _1[0 of 1];`, `[[rhs:_.*]] = copy _2[0 of 1];`, and `_0 = Cmp(move [[lhs]], move [[rhs]]);`. Emit and inspect both panic strategies. Also verify the guard by checking that general operand/rvalue replacement does not introduce new `Deref` or non-stable `Index` projections, while aggregate reconstruction may still use complex projections.
